fixes.cover: Senior staff at HMAS Leeuwin knew of the abuse and tolerated it; in 2000 a 15-year-old Air Force cadet faced disciplinary proceedings and discharge after an adult instructor's inappropriate relationship with her, which the commission said should never have happened.

note: Royal Commission media release confirms Leeuwin (1960s-1972, senior staff knew and tolerated), Balcombe (1970s-80s hierarchy) and AAFC age-of-consent-14 policy since at least 2000; minister's 18 June 2014 statement confirms 200+ junior recruits aged 15-17. Reworded cover: the 15-year-old cadet faced disciplinary proceedings and discharge, which the commission said she should not have.

fixes.d: Former Supreme Court Justice Margaret Nyland led a two-year royal commission into South Australia's child protection system, set up in 2014 after Families SA carer Shannon McCoole was charged with sexual offences against children in his care; McCoole was later jailed for 35 years. Her report, 'The Life They Deserve', was delivered to the Governor on 5 August 2016 with 260 recommendations. It found that many children in state care had been abused and neglected not only by their families but also let down by the system meant to protect them.

note: SA government page confirms report name, 5 Aug 2016 delivery and 260 recommendations; SBS confirms Nyland, two-year inquiry and McCoole's 35-year term. Fixed sequence: the commission was set up in 2014 after McCoole was charged; he was sentenced to 35 years in August 2015, during the inquiry.

Report PDF confirms appointment 22 Nov 2011, 19 offences/5 boys (1991), 10 more (2011), 29 offences against 11 boys aged 14-16, offending 1977-1990, adverse findings against one police officer and one councillor, and that officials mostly took no action. Report gives McKenna's wardenship as 1975 (acting) / 1976 to 1990, so d left as is.

AP/Deseret confirms chair Lalieux, unanimous approval 30 March 2011, abuse in every sector esp. boarding schools, at least 13 suicides, arbitration body and 10-to-15-year limitation recommendation. Belgian bishops' conference history (bwcatho.be) confirms the Adriaenssens commission ended with the June 2010 seizures (Operation Calice) and the arbitration centre's rules adopted Dec 2011/Jan 2012.

fixes.who: Networks including politicians, businessmen and clergy named by the commission
fixes.d: A joint commission of 11 senators and 11 deputies, created in 2003 to investigate violence and networks of sexual exploitation of children and adolescents, had by May 2004 received more than 800 complaints, heard more than 300 people and visited 14 states. Its final report, approved on 13 July 2004, put more than 250 people on notice, among them 20 serving politicians (including one federal deputy, two state deputies and three mayors), about 30 businessmen and five priests, and passed the cases to federal and state prosecutors. The commission's bill rewriting the Penal Code chapter on 'crimes against public morals' (PLS 253/2004) became Law 12.015 of 2009.

note: Senate library record confirms report and officers; Al Jazeera confirms 250+ put on notice, 20 politicians (1 federal deputy, 2 state deputies, 3 mayors), 30 businessmen, 5 priests, 13 July 2004 vote. Saboya's 12 May 2004 speech gives 800+ complaints, 300+ heard, 14 states visited (interim figures). Judges were not named in the sources, so removed from 'who'; the unverified 'internal trafficking' recommendation was replaced with the CPMI's bill PLS 253/2004, which the Senate record says became Law 12.015/2009.

Global News confirms 3 Dec 2020 tabling, 18 months, hearings in Quebec City, Montreal and Val-d'Or, about 600 establishments, Montreal hub, pimps up to $300,000 a year, 58 recommendations and the 'national priority' first recommendation.

Mapping report page confirms 'apparent systematic use of rape and sexual assault' by all forces, rape of Hutu refugee women and children 1996-97, rape and torture of child soldiers in camps, and the 12 parties in the SG's footnote; UN News confirms 1 Oct 2010 release. Kinshasa is a representative point for a country-wide report.

fixes.d: After the 2010 revelations at Canisius-Kolleg and other schools, the federal government appointed former minister Christine Bergmann as Independent Commissioner. Her final report, presented on 24 May 2011 to the Round Table on Child Sexual Abuse, drew on about 13,000 letters and 2,000 phone calls from victims and relatives about abuse in churches, schools, sports clubs and families. It recommended that institutions where abuse occurred make one-time payments based on what courts would award, that therapy costs be covered, and that an independent body oversee implementation. A permanent federal commissioner's office followed, and in 2016 an Independent Commission for the investigation of child sexual abuse began work.

note: epd/evangelisch.de confirms 24 May 2011, about 13,000 letters and 2,000 calls, settings (churches, schools, sports clubs, families), institutional payments at court-award level, therapy costs and an independent follow-up body. Reworded the last sentence as a sequence of events rather than direct causation; note setting 'religious' is broader than churches.

JLU press release confirms Maschke/Stecher, Marburg and Giessen, 5 Feb 2026, structural problem, camps and trips, male leaders and female minors, looking away and downplaying, DPSG accepting institutional failure; epd confirms Cologne, 1929-2022, over 90% male accused, mainly girls and young women, not representative.

fixes.cover: The study faulted Cardinal Karl Lehmann's early years (1983–2001) as 'deflecting and dissembling' and also criticised Bishop Albert Stohr and Cardinal Hermann Volk; Bishop Peter Kohlgraf said that for his predecessors protecting perpetrators and the Church mattered more than those affected.
fixes.d: The study 'Erfahren. Verstehen. Vorsorgen.' by lawyer Ulrich Weber, commissioned by the diocese, was released on 3 March 2023. It identified 657 possible victims and 392 suspects for 1945 to 2019, of whom 401 victims and 181 accused remained after review. Weber said Cardinal Karl Lehmann, bishop from 1983 to 2016, never met his own public standard for handling abuse. Bishop Peter Kohlgraf acknowledged major misconduct and omissions under Lehmann, Cardinal Hermann Volk and earlier leaders.
fixes.cite: Ulrich Weber, 'Erfahren. Verstehen. Vorsorgen.' (EVV), Diocese of Mainz, 3 March 2023 (The Pillar via BishopAccountability, 4 March 2023)

note: The Pillar (via BishopAccountability) confirms 3 March 2023, 1945-2019, 657/392 and 401/181, Lehmann's 1983-2001 'deflecting and dissembling' phase and Weber's 'never fulfilled his own claim'. The 'protecting perpetrators mattered more' statement was Bishop Kohlgraf's, not the study's; cover and cite corrected. Commissioning year 2019 and co-author Baumeister not in the opened source, removed.

epd confirms commission working since 2021, report in Munich on 2 Oct 2024, 226 cases (189 via internal office, 37 after a 2023 newspaper appeal), rape in individual cases, about half by staff and about 20% by other young people, 'closed family units are a risk', more unrecorded cases likely.

JURIST confirms Appeals Board/Ministry report, 1970-1989, 7,220 children, 'systematic illegal behavior' by Korean organisations, money exchanged, DanAdopt and AC Børnehjælp knew of altered information, and adoptee group criticism of the state's role.

Forces News (4 July 2017) confirms 363 allegations 2012-2017, 282 referred to police, 99 instructors dismissed, over £2m paid, victims discouraged from going to police, former cadets abused in the 1980s, MoD response.

Committee press release confirms HC 68-I, 10 June 2013, shared failure of police, social services and CPS, Rochdale and Rotherham 'lack of professional curiosity', the localised grooming model as only one of several, and court reform recommendations. The record's url is a parliament 'webtest' mirror; the www.parliament.uk equivalent could not be opened (permission prompt timed out), so url kept.

fixes.victims_note: At least 57 victims and 97 potential suspects identified by Operation Augusta; the later Operation Green Jacket identified 53 potential victims, 48 of them in council care.
fixes.cover: Senior officers closed the investigation in July 2005; minutes of the meetings on its closure disappeared and several officials declined to cooperate with the review.
fixes.d: An assurance review commissioned by Greater Manchester Mayor Andy Burnham, published 14 January 2020, found that Operation Augusta, set up in 2004 after the death of a 15-year-old girl in council care, had identified at least 57 victims and 97 potential suspects before senior officers closed it in July 2005. Allegations of rape and abuse were not followed up and very few perpetrators were brought to justice; some suspects visited council children's homes apparently with staff knowledge. Minutes of the closure meetings were missing.

note: ITV and the GMCA review confirm Burnham's commission, 14 Jan 2020, Augusta set up 2004 after the death of a 15-year-old girl in care, 57 victims and 97 suspects, missing closure minutes, suspects visiting homes with staff knowledge, Green Jacket 53/48, officials declining to cooperate. Review says Augusta was closed 1 July 2005 and covered exploitation from early 2002, with concerns passed to police and social services in 2002; y0 and first_report changed to 2002. 'Under-resourced' and 'aged 12-16' not confirmed, removed.

CYP Now confirms 4 Feb 2015, 'not fit for purpose', denial, CSE treated as a social care issue, taxi licensing (86% inadequate), 'some lengths' to conceal information and silence whistleblowers, severance/compromise agreements. Cabinet resignation and commissioners confirmed by ITV (4 Feb 2015) and Local Government Lawyer headlines; added ITV as url2.

cite: Scottish Child Abuse Inquiry, thirteenth volume of case study findings: Queen Victoria School, Dunblane, 22 October 2024
note: SCAI news page confirms 22 Oct 2024, 13th volume, 'dreadful abuse' late 1950s to early 1990s, culture of silence and military culture, teacher employed 1973-1993 whose behaviour was well known but the school took no action, and a drumming instructor who abused seven girls 2011-2019. It is not Case Study no. 9; cite corrected.

fixes.d: Tom Shaw, former chief inspector of education in Northern Ireland, reviewed for the Scottish Executive the laws, rules and records governing residential schools and children's homes from 1950 to 1995; his report was published in November 2007. He found the regulations were 'extensive and in many respects impressive' but that successive governments and authorities failed to make sure they were followed, and that abuse would likely have been less common had they been honoured. About 35 former residents were interviewed and about 80 other people gave evidence. He recommended a national task group, a centre for former residents and new law on children's home records.

note: Scotsman and Community Care confirm Shaw's background, 1950-1995 scope, ~35 victims interviewed and 80 others, Nazareth House and Quarriers, regulations 'extensive' but not followed, and abuse likely lower had they been honoured. The sentence that survivors described mental, physical and sexual abuse was not in either source and was replaced.

fixes.d: John Jillings led an investigation into abuse in Clwyd County Council's children's homes; the report was finished in 1996, withheld because the council's insurers feared compensation claims, and published in redacted form in July 2013. It found abuse in Clwyd homes was 'extensive and has taken place over a substantial number of years' and that responses were 'too little and too late'. It criticised North Wales Police for investigating allegations against its own officers and said the council and other agencies gave limited information, some refusing to meet the panel. It called for a judicial inquiry; the Waterhouse tribunal later examined the wider abuse.

note: Scotsman confirms 1996 compilation, publication after 17 years in redacted form, 'extensive', 'too little and too late', police investigating own officers, limited information and refusals to meet, 3,755 statements, at least 24 victims, call for a judicial inquiry. Jillings' job title not in the source, removed; the link to Waterhouse softened. Note: y0/y1 1963-1992 are Operation Pallial's range for North Wales homes; the Scotsman says the report covered the 1970s and 1980s.

Irish Times confirms 1,496 of about 150,000 records sampled, about 265 files with markers, estimate 5,540-19,980, Tusla's evidence of coerced consent, children placed abroad and altered names/dates, no call for a full review. TheJournal (30 May 2018) confirms 126 St Patrick's Guild cases registered 1946-1969; added y0/y1.

fixes.d: An investigative commission of the Catholic Church in Iceland, chaired by Hjördís Hákonardóttir, reported in early November 2012. It confirmed that Rev. Ágúst Georg, principal of the church's Landakotsskóli school, and teacher Margrét Müller abused pupils. Of 30 former pupils and summer-camp children questioned, 8 said they had been sexually abused and 27 described mental abuse. It found that Bishop Joannes Gijsen destroyed a letter reporting abuse by the priest. In December 2015 the Althing passed Act No. 117/2015, extending the state compensation scheme for abuse in institutions to Landakotsskóli.

note: BishopAccountability/Iceland Review (5 Nov 2012) confirms chair, priest and teacher, 30 questioned, 8 sexual abuse, 27 mental abuse, Bishop Gijsen destroying a letter. Compensation claim checked against Althing Act No. 117/2015, which opened the state compensation scheme to Landakotsskóli claims; d reworded and added as url2.

'National Task Force' title kept as in record; sources call it a ministry team.

fixes.cite: Witness to Truth: Report of the Sierra Leone Truth and Reconciliation Commission (2004), chapter 'Women and the Armed Conflict' (excerpts compiled by McMaster University Truth Commissions Digital Collection); TRC overview, October 2004 (ReliefWeb)
fixes.victims_note: 2,058 abductions of women and girls reported to the TRC; 189 allegations of sexual slavery (72.5% attributed to the RUF, 11.6% to the AFRC)
fixes.d: The Truth and Reconciliation Commission of Sierra Leone released its final report in October 2004. It found that the RUF and the AFRC 'deliberately embarked on systematic strategies to abduct and rape women and girls between the ages of ten and 14 years', using them as sexual and domestic slaves and 'wives'; in a few cases the children were below ten. It also found that the CDF carried out a deliberate strategy of rape, sexual slavery and other sexual violations against girls, and that girls as young as 12 were forced to pay for aid with sex. Of 189 allegations of sexual slavery of women and girls reported to it, 72.5% were attributed to the RUF and 11.6% to the AFRC.

note: McMaster excerpts confirm the RUF/AFRC 'ten and 14 years' quote, victims below ten in a few cases, CDF strategy against girls, girls as young as 12 forced to pay for aid with sex, and 189 sexual slavery allegations (72.5% RUF, 11.6% AFRC); the attribution of the 2,058 abductions is cut off in the source, so the last sentence was narrowed. The 5 Oct 2004 Security Council presentation date rests on the Wikipedia url2; ReliefWeb's Oct 2004 overview confirms the report but not the day, so date changed to October 2004 and url2 swapped to ReliefWeb.

AP via The Columbian (1 March 2016) confirms 50+ priests and religious leaders, hundreds of children, about 40 years, two bishops including Joseph Adamec, and help selecting a police chief.

ABC Action News confirms 6 Nov 2020 closure, two-year probe opened after the 2018 Pennsylvania report, 260+ tips, 97 priests none prosecutable, Florida as a place accused priests were 'routinely relocated' (81 listed), church acts enabling abuse and obstructing discovery, no ongoing abuse found.

fixes.d: Iowa Attorney General Tom Miller's office released its review on 23 June 2021 after an inquiry begun in late 2018. It examined 50 complaints, 45 involving the Catholic Church, with records involving 70 priests and alleged abuse from the 1930s to 1997. It described a painful history of abuse and extensive cover-ups in Iowa's Catholic dioceses but found the four dioceses had made reforms in good faith over the past two decades. None of the complaints against Catholic clergy could be prosecuted because of the statute of limitations.

note: Iowa Public Radio confirms late-2018 start, June 2021 release, 50 complaints (45 Catholic), 70 priests, 1930s to 1997, cover-ups, good-faith reforms, statute of limitations, survivors saying allegations were ignored or covered up. The word 'overwhelming' is not in the source; d reworded.

Michigan AG releases confirm all report dates, Oct 2018 warrants at all seven dioceses, Saginaw 37 priests + 1 deacon, Grand Rapids 51 priests, 1,276 tips, 11 cases, 9 convictions, 38 survivors, disclaimer, Detroit pending, allegations since 1950. Lansing 56 accused / 48 priests confirmed by CBS Detroit and other headlines.

America magazine confirms Nov 2020 suit, more than two dozen priests protected by not sending cases to the Vatican, Malone and Grosz, settlement filed 25 Oct 2022, enhanced measures, independent compliance auditor, bishops barred from fiduciary roles in New York.

MPR News confirms June 2015 six gross misdemeanor child endangerment counts, three brothers abused by Wehmeyer, charges dropped 20 July 2016 with the quoted admission, December 2015 civil settlement with oversight to February 2020.

fixes.cover: Complaints at the West Texas State School from 2001 to 2005 were largely ignored; a TYC headquarters inquiry found no abuse; the local district attorney never took the Texas Rangers' case to a grand jury
fixes.d: A Texas Ranger's 229-page report documented sexual abuse of boys by two senior administrators at the West Texas State School in Pyote, where complaints from 2001 to 2005 had been largely ignored and the local prosecutor did not take the case to a grand jury; the two were indicted in April 2007. When this became public in February 2007, investigators counted more than 750 sexual abuse complaints across all 13 Texas Youth Commission facilities from January 2000 to February 2007. The TYC board resigned on 16 March 2007, the legislature approved a conservator for the agency, and by May 2007, 93 employees had been suspended, fired or forced to retire.

note: Prison Legal News confirms the 229-page Ranger report, two administrators at Pyote, TYC HQ inquiry clearing them, DA never presenting to a grand jury, 750+ complaints at all 13 facilities Jan 2000-Feb 2007, board resignation 16 March 2007, conservator, 93 employees by May 2007. Complaints were ignored from 2001 (not 2003) to 2005; first_report, cover and d corrected.

CBS/AP (20 June 2002) confirms 13 pages, two months, tens of thousands of pages, eight alleged victims, the 'orchestrated effort' quote, felony for failure to report, ending the statute of limitations for minors, and the archdiocese calling it unfair.
